title: Part B: percakapan panjang — konteks, urutan & angka
title_target: Longer conversations — topic, sequence, and what happens next
goal: Mengikuti percakapan dua menit tanpa mencatat: menangkap topiknya dari kalimat-kalimat pembuka, menjawab soal detail sambil percakapan terus berjalan, dan tidak kehilangan dua soal berikutnya saat satu soal lewat.
bekal: menebak situasi percakapan dari pilihan jawaban sebelum audionya menyala
membedakan angka yang jadi jawaban dari angka yang cuma disebut
menjawab soal 'what will the student probably do next' dari dua baris terakhir

sections.title: Part B: dua percakapan panjang, tanpa catatan, tanpa soal tercetak

blocks.text: Part B adalah **dua percakapan panjang**, masing-masing sekitar 1,5–2 menit, yang diputar tepat setelah 30 percakapan pendek Part A. Penuturnya hampir selalu orang kampus: mahasiswa dengan dosen, penasihat akademik, petugas perpustakaan, teknisi laboratorium, atau pegawai kantor pendaftaran. Dari dua percakapan itu keluar **7–9 soal** — biasanya empat atau lima per percakapan, nomor 31 sampai kira-kira 38.

Dua aturan membuat Part B terasa lebih berat daripada ukurannya. Pertama, **kamu tidak boleh mencatat** — buku soal tidak boleh dicoret, dan pensil hanya untuk lembar jawaban. Kedua, **pertanyaannya tidak tercetak**. Di buku soal hanya ada empat pilihan (A)–(D); pertanyaannya dibacakan narator satu kali sesudah percakapan selesai, lalu kamu punya sekitar 12 detik untuk menjawab sebelum pertanyaan berikutnya dibacakan.

Jadi yang kamu pegang selama dua menit itu hanya ingatan dan deretan pilihan jawaban. Kabar baiknya: penulis soal tahu itu, dan mereka menyusun soalnya **mengikuti urutan percakapan**. Soal pertama hampir selalu tentang topik atau tujuan, soal-soal tengah tentang detail sesuai urutan munculnya, dan soal terakhir tentang apa yang akan terjadi sesudah percakapan. Urutan itulah pegangan utamamu.

blocks.title: Cara memakai unit ini
items: Audio Part B ada di menu **Simulasi**, diputar sekali seperti tes asli. Unit ini melatih yang bisa disiapkan sebelum audio menyala: membaca pilihan, menebak situasi, dan tahu jenis soal apa yang datang di urutan ke berapa.

Urutannya: (1) baca pilihan jawaban semua soal di Latihan 1 — jangan pertanyaannya, karena di tes asli pertanyaan tidak ada; (2) tulis satu kalimat tebakanmu tentang situasinya; (3) baru baca Transkrip 1 **satu kali, dari atas ke bawah, tanpa mengulang**, lalu jawab. Ulangi untuk Transkrip 2.
Saat membaca transkrip, jangan berhenti untuk mencari jawaban soal 2 kalau kamu sudah sampai bagian soal 4. Di tes asli, audio tidak berhenti.

sections.title: Yang diuji: lima jenis soal, dan di mana jawabannya bersembunyi

blocks.text: Dari puluhan tes TOEFL ITP yang pernah diterbitkan, soal Part B jatuh ke lima jenis yang sama. Yang penting bukan menghafal namanya, tapi tahu **di bagian mana percakapan** jawaban tiap jenis biasanya diletakkan.

head: Jenis soal
Bunyi pertanyaannya
Di mana jawabannya
rows: Topik atau tujuan
*What is the conversation mainly about? · Why did the student go to see the advisor?*
Dua–tiga kalimat pertama. Mahasiswa hampir selalu menyebut urusannya di baris pertama atau kedua (*I emailed you about my schedule*, *I'd like to borrow some equipment*).
Detail berurutan
*What does the woman say about the meters? · According to the man, why…?*
Tersebar di tubuh percakapan, dalam urutan yang sama dengan nomor soal. Jawaban soal 33 tidak pernah ada sebelum jawaban soal 32.
Angka, waktu, tempat
*When is the deadline? · How many credits…? · Where should the student go?*
Biasanya disebut lebih dari satu angka yang mirip (tiga tanggal, dua hari). Yang jadi jawaban sering yang disebut **terakhir** atau yang **diulang** oleh penutur lain.
Langkah berikutnya
*What will the student probably do next? · What does the man suggest the woman do?*
Dua–tiga baris terakhir. Dengarkan kalimat mahasiswa yang berbunyi *So I'll…* atau *All right, I'll try to…* — itu jawabannya, bukan saran-saran yang disebut di tengah.
Sikap atau pendapat
*How does the advisor feel about the student's plan? · What does the man imply about…?*
Bukan di satu kalimat, tapi di kata penilai yang berserakan: *I'd worry about…*, *that's the issue*, *honestly*, *not a problem*. Nada suara juga dihitung.

blocks.text: Perhatikan bahwa **empat dari lima jenis soal punya alamat**. Kalau kamu tahu soal 31 selalu tentang tujuan, kamu tidak perlu menunggu seluruh percakapan untuk menjawabnya — kamu sudah bisa memegangnya di detik kelima belas, dan sisa perhatianmu bebas untuk soal berikutnya.

Satu hal lagi tentang pengecoh. Penulis soal Part B tahu kamu mendengar sepotong-sepotong, jadi tiga pilihan salah biasanya dibangun dari **kata yang memang diucapkan** — tanggal yang sudah lewat, saran yang ditolak, angka dari kalimat lain. Pilihan yang 'terdengar familiar' bukan jaminan benar; pilihan yang benar adalah yang cocok dengan **kalimat lengkapnya**.

sections.title: Strategi: pilihan jawaban adalah satu-satunya teks yang kamu punya

items: **Baca ke depan saat narator bicara.** Instruksi Part B dibacakan sekitar 30 detik, dan itu waktu paling berharga di seluruh section. Pakai untuk membaca pilihan jawaban empat–lima soal pertama. Dua puluh frasa pendek — kamu sanggup.

**Tebak situasinya dari kata yang berulang di pilihan.** Kalau di beberapa soal muncul *withdraw*, *credits*, *transcript*, *deadline*, kamu tahu ini urusan akademik dengan penasihat, dan kamu tahu akan ada tanggal. Kalau muncul *reserve*, *return*, *sign out*, ini soal peminjaman. Tebakan ini membuat kalimat pertama percakapan langsung terpasang di tempatnya.

**Saat audio berjalan, mata di pilihan soal yang sedang berlangsung.** Kamu tidak mencatat, jadi biarkan pilihan jawaban menjadi catatannya. Begitu kamu mendengar frasa yang cocok dengan salah satu pilihan — atau yang membantahnya — tandai di kepala dan geser mata ke soal berikutnya.

**Kalimat pertama dan kedua: pegang topiknya, jangan tunggu.** Mahasiswa TOEFL tidak berbasa-basi lama. *I'm thinking about switching my major* di baris ketiga adalah jawaban soal 31, dan tidak akan diulang.

**Untuk angka, tunggu kalimatnya selesai.** *The deadline to drop without a W was September thirtieth, so that's passed. You can still withdraw until November fifteenth.* Dua tanggal; yang pertama sudah lewat. Penulis soal hampir selalu memberi angka umpan sebelum angka jawaban.

**Kalau satu soal lewat, isi apa saja dan pindah.** Tidak ada pengurangan nilai untuk jawaban salah. Soal yang kosong sudah pasti nol; soal yang ditebak masih 25 persen — dan soal berikutnya masih 100 persen kalau kamu sudah ada di sana saat jawabannya diucapkan.

blocks.title: Tiga kebiasaan yang menghabiskan soal Part B
items: **Mengejar satu soal.** Peserta yang tidak yakin soal 33 lalu memutar ulang percakapan di kepalanya kehilangan 34 dan 35. Ini kerugian paling umum di Part B, dan paling mudah dihindari: satu tebakan, satu gerakan mata ke bawah.

**Mencoba mengingat semuanya.** Kamu tidak perlu ingat nama dosen, nama gedung, atau nomor ruangan kalau tidak ada di pilihan jawaban. Pilihan jawaban memberi tahu **apa yang layak diingat** — dengarkan selektif.

**Menjawab dari pengetahuan umum.** *A W is not calculated into your GPA* mungkin berbeda dari aturan kampusmu. Yang dinilai adalah apa yang dikatakan penutur, bukan apa yang benar di dunia nyata. Pengecoh 'masuk akal tapi tidak disebut' dibuat persis untuk peserta yang menjawab dari luar percakapan.

blocks.text: Cuplikan pendek dari percakapan mahasiswa dengan petugas kantor asrama. Tabel di bawahnya menunjukkan empat soal yang biasa ditanyakan dari cuplikan sependek ini, dan pengecoh yang dipasang di tiap soal.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Hi. I'm here about the notice on my door. It says my room is scheduled for an inspection tomorrow, and I don't know what that means.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, that's nothing to worry about. All the rooms on the third floor are being checked for smoke detectors this week. It only takes about ten minutes, but somebody has to be in the room to let the technician in.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: That's the problem. I have a lab tomorrow from nine to noon, and I can't miss it.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: No problem. The technician is here all day. I'll put you down for the afternoon slot, between one and three. Just make sure you're back by one.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I will. Thanks.

head: Soal
Jawaban
Pengecoh & alasan
rows: Why did the woman go to the housing office?
To ask about a notice she received
Baris pertama: *I'm here about the notice on my door.* Pengecoh *to report a broken smoke detector* memakai kata *smoke detector* dari percakapan, tapi tidak ada yang rusak.
What will happen in the woman's room tomorrow?
A smoke detector will be checked
*being checked for smoke detectors.* Pengecoh *the room will be cleaned* masuk akal untuk kata *inspection* tapi tidak disebut; *the woman will move to another floor* bertentangan.
Why can't the woman be in her room in the morning?
She has a class
*I have a lab tomorrow from nine to noon.* Pengecoh *she works in the afternoon* menukar waktunya; *she will be out of town* tidak disebut.
What will the man probably do?
Schedule the inspection for the afternoon
*I'll put you down for the afternoon slot.* Pengecoh *cancel the inspection* bertentangan dengan *no problem, the technician is here all day*.

blocks.text: Empat soal, empat alamat: baris pertama, baris kedua, baris ketiga, baris terakhir. Percakapan Part B yang sebenarnya lima kali lebih panjang, tapi polanya tidak berubah — soal hanya bergeser ke bawah mengikuti percakapan.

Berhenti di sini. Buka **Latihan 1**, baca hanya pilihan jawabannya, dan tulis satu kalimat tebakan tentang situasi percakapannya. Baru baca Transkrip 1 **satu kali, tanpa mengulang** — dalam kecepatan bicara normal, percakapan ini sekitar dua menit. Kerjakan Latihan 1, lalu ulangi langkah yang sama untuk Transkrip 2 dan Latihan 2.

blocks.title: Conversation 1: A student visits an academic advisor

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Hi, Dr. Alvarez? I'm Kevin Park. I emailed you yesterday about my schedule.

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: Yes, Kevin, come in. You wanted to talk about dropping a class, is that right?

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Sort of. I'm in Organic Chemistry this semester, and honestly, I'm drowning. I got a 58 on the first exam. I'm thinking about switching my major from biology to environmental studies, and I'm not sure I even need the class.

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: Let's take those one at a time. First, the class. Today is October tenth. The deadline to drop a course without it showing on your transcript was September thirtieth, so that's passed. You can still withdraw until November fifteenth, but you'd get a W on your record.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Does a W hurt my GPA?

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: No, it isn't calculated into your GPA at all. Graduate schools notice a pattern of W's, but a single one isn't a problem. What I'd worry about more is your credit load. If you withdraw, how many credits are you left with?

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Eleven, I think. Chemistry is four credits.

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: That's the issue. You need twelve to stay a full-time student, and your scholarship requires full-time status. Dropping chemistry without adding something else would put your scholarship at risk.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: I didn't know that. Could I add a class this late?

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: Not a regular one, no. But there are several one-credit short courses that start in the second half of the semester — the eight-week session begins October twentieth. A one-credit seminar would bring you back up to twelve.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Okay. And what about changing majors? Would environmental studies still require organic chemistry?

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: It doesn't. The environmental studies program requires only general chemistry, which you've already completed. But changing majors isn't something you do this afternoon. You fill out a change-of-major form, get it signed by the chair of the new department, and submit it to the registrar. The department accepts new majors only twice a year, and the next window closes November first.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: So I'd have about three weeks.

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: Right. And before you decide, I'd like you to talk to Professor Whitfield. She directs the environmental studies program, and she can tell you which of your biology credits will transfer. Most of them will, but not all.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Should I withdraw from chemistry first, or talk to her first?

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: Talk to her first. If you end up staying in biology, you'll need that course eventually, and a tutor might be a better answer than a W. The tutoring center has free sessions for organic chemistry every evening.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: All right. I'll try to see Professor Whitfield this week. Thank you, Dr. Alvarez.

lines.speaker: Advisor
lines.text: Good luck, Kevin. Come back and let me know what you decide.

blocks.title: Conversation 2: A student borrows equipment from a laboratory

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Excuse me, is this the equipment room for the geology department?

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: It is. I'm Ray, the lab technician. What can I do for you?

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: My name is Dana Okafor. I'm doing an independent research project with Professor Lindqvist, and she said I could borrow some field equipment from here. I need to collect water samples from Miller Creek.

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: Sure. Do you have the authorization form? Anything that leaves this room needs a signature from a faculty member.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: She signed it this morning. Here.

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: Great. What do you need?

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: A GPS unit, a set of sample bottles, and one of the digital water-testing meters — the kind that measures pH and temperature.

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: The bottles and the GPS aren't a problem. The meters are another story. We have six, but four of them are reserved for the hydrology class on Tuesdays and Thursdays, so those two days are out. The other two are available, but only on a first-come basis.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: I was planning to go out on Thursday morning.

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: Then you'd need to come by Wednesday afternoon and take one before the class signs them out. Otherwise you'll be waiting until Friday.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Wednesday afternoon, then. How long can I keep everything?

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: Bottles, as long as you need. The GPS and the meter have a three-day limit during the semester. If your fieldwork runs longer, you can renew, but you have to bring the equipment back in and let me check it. Last year a student kept a meter for two weeks and the battery corroded, so now we check.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Three days is fine. I only need one full day at the creek. Do I need to calibrate the meter myself?

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: I'll calibrate it before you pick it up, but it takes about twenty minutes, so don't come at five minutes to closing. We close at four thirty. And take the instruction card — the meter gives you a reading in Celsius, and I've seen students record it as Fahrenheit and ruin a whole data set.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Good to know. One more thing. The professor mentioned that the department has a small fund for transportation to field sites. Do you handle that?

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: No, that's the department office, second floor. Ask for the field travel form. They reimburse mileage, but you have to submit receipts within thirty days of the trip.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Perfect. So I'll go upstairs now, and I'll come back Wednesday for the equipment.

lines.speaker: Technician
lines.text: Sounds good. And Dana — bring a printed copy of the authorization form on Wednesday. I'll keep the one you gave me on file, but I need another for the sign-out sheet.

lines.speaker: Student
lines.text: Will do. Thanks, Ray.

exercises.prompt: Questions 1–5. Conversation 1. Read the conversation ONCE, then choose the best answer to each question. Di tes asli pertanyaannya hanya dibacakan; di sini dicetak supaya bisa kamu periksa.
items: What is the student's main problem? (A) He missed the deadline to register for a chemistry class. (B) He is doing poorly in a course and is considering changing his major. (C) He has already lost his scholarship because of a low grade. (D) He wants to take a class that is not offered this semester. ____
What is the last day the student can withdraw from the course? (A) September 30 (B) October 10 (C) October 20 (D) November 15 ____

Why is the advisor concerned about the student withdrawing from chemistry? (A) The student would fall below the number of credits required for his scholarship. (B) A W on the transcript would lower the student's grade point average. (C) The student would have to take general chemistry again. (D) Graduate schools do not accept students with a W on their records. ____

What does the advisor say about the environmental studies program? (A) It requires students to complete organic chemistry. (B) It accepts new majors at any time during the year. (C) It does not accept any credits from the biology department. (D) The chair of the department must sign the change-of-major form. ____
What will the student probably do next? (A) Withdraw from organic chemistry (B) Register for a one-credit seminar (C) Talk to Professor Whitfield (D) Sign up for evening tutoring ____

exercises.prompt: Questions 6–11. Conversation 2. Read the conversation ONCE, then choose the best answer to each question.
items: Why does the woman go to the equipment room? (A) To register for a hydrology class (B) To return some equipment she borrowed last week (C) To borrow equipment for a research project (D) To ask about a job as a laboratory assistant ____

What does the man say about the water-testing meters? (A) Most of them are reserved for a class on certain days. (B) All of them are being repaired at the moment. (C) Only faculty members are allowed to borrow them. (D) They can be kept for up to two weeks. ____
When will the woman pick up the equipment? (A) Tuesday morning (B) Wednesday afternoon (C) Thursday morning (D) Friday afternoon ____

Why does the man mention a student from last year? (A) To recommend a good place to collect samples (B) To explain why equipment must be checked before it is renewed (C) To warn that the department does not supply batteries (D) To show that most students return equipment late ____

What does the man warn the woman about? (A) The meter shows temperature in Celsius. (B) The meter must be calibrated at the creek. (C) The instruction card has been lost. (D) The equipment room closes early on Wednesdays. ____
What will the woman probably do next? (A) Calibrate the meter (B) Print a copy of the authorization form (C) Go to the department office (D) Drive to Miller Creek ____

answers: C — A — B — B — A — C

head: No
Jawaban
Alasan & pengecoh
rows: B

Baris ketiga: *I'm drowning. I got a 58 on the first exam. I'm thinking about switching my major.* Dua masalah dalam satu napas, dan (B) memuat keduanya. (A) memakai kata *deadline* yang memang ada, tapi tenggat yang dibahas adalah *drop*, bukan *register*. (C) bertentangan: beasiswanya *at risk*, belum hilang. (D) tidak disebut sama sekali.
D

*You can still withdraw until November fifteenth.* Tiga tanggal lain semuanya diucapkan dan semuanya umpan: *October tenth* adalah hari ini, *September thirtieth* tenggat yang *passed*, *October twentieth* awal sesi delapan minggu. Soal angka Part B hampir selalu dibangun begini — empat angka yang semuanya benar-benar terdengar.
A

*You need twelve to stay a full-time student, and your scholarship requires full-time status.* (B) bertentangan langsung: *it isn't calculated into your GPA at all*. (D) melebih-lebihkan: penasihat bilang *a single one isn't a problem*. (C) tidak pernah disebut — general chemistry justru *already completed*.
D

*get it signed by the chair of the new department.* (A) bertentangan: *It doesn't.* (B) bertentangan: *only twice a year*. (C) bertentangan dengan *Most of them will, but not all* — sebagian besar kredit diterima. Perhatikan bahwa tiga pengecohnya semua memakai isi percakapan yang dibalik.
C

Baris kedua dari akhir: *All right. I'll try to see Professor Whitfield this week.* Ketiga pengecoh adalah hal yang **dibahas** tapi belum diputuskan: withdraw (ditunda: *talk to her first*), seminar satu kredit (baru kalau ia withdraw), tutor (saran, bukan rencana). Soal *probably do next* selalu dijawab dari kalimat rencana mahasiswa, bukan dari daftar saran penasihat.
C

Baris ketiga: *I'm doing an independent research project… she said I could borrow some field equipment.* (A) memakai *hydrology class* yang muncul belakangan tentang jadwal meteran, bukan tentang si mahasiswa. (B) menukar arah: ia meminjam, bukan mengembalikan. (D) tidak disebut.
A

*We have six, but four of them are reserved for the hydrology class on Tuesdays and Thursdays.* Empat dari enam = sebagian besar. (B) tidak disebut. (C) menyimpangkan aturan *needs a signature from a faculty member* — yang diperlukan tanda tangan dosen, bukan peminjamnya harus dosen. (D) bertentangan: *a three-day limit*; *two weeks* adalah lama mahasiswa tahun lalu menahan alat, bukan batasnya.
B

*Then you'd need to come by Wednesday afternoon… — Wednesday afternoon, then.* Diucapkan dua kali, oleh dua penutur: tanda kuat jawaban. *Thursday morning* adalah rencana ke lapangan, bukan hari mengambil alat; *Tuesday* hari kelas hidrologi; *Friday* pilihan kalau ia terlambat.
B

*If your fieldwork runs longer, you can renew, but you have to bring the equipment back in and let me check it. Last year a student kept a meter for two weeks and the battery corroded, so now we check.* Fungsinya adalah **alasan** untuk aturan pemeriksaan. (C) memakai kata *battery* tapi soal baterai tidak disediakan tidak pernah dibahas. (D) menggeneralisasi satu kejadian menjadi kebiasaan.
A

*the meter gives you a reading in Celsius, and I've seen students record it as Fahrenheit.* (B) bertentangan: *I'll calibrate it before you pick it up*. (C) bertentangan: kartunya ada, *take the instruction card*. (D) tidak disebut — ruangan tutup *four thirty* setiap hari, tidak ada yang khusus Rabu.
C

*So I'll go upstairs now.* Lantai atas = *the department office, second floor*, tempat formulir perjalanan lapangan. (B) adalah hal yang harus ia lakukan Rabu, bukan sekarang. (A) dikerjakan teknisi. (D) baru Kamis. Jawaban soal terakhir ada di kalimat *So I'll…* — persis seperti pola yang dibahas di tabel jenis soal.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat dari dua percakapan ini
items: Soal 2 dan 8 adalah soal angka, dan keduanya dibangun dengan cara yang sama: **semua pilihan benar-benar diucapkan**. Yang membedakan jawaban dari umpan bukan 'pernah dengar atau tidak', tapi konteks kalimatnya — *so that's passed*, *then you'd need to come by*. Kalau kamu hanya mengingat angka tanpa kalimatnya, empat pilihan terasa sama benarnya.

Soal 5 dan 11 (*what will the student probably do next*) sama-sama dijawab dari kalimat **rencana** mahasiswa (*I'll try to…*, *So I'll…*), bukan dari daftar saran yang disebut di tengah. Tiga pengecohnya selalu diambil dari daftar saran itu — semuanya memang dibahas, dan tidak satu pun yang dipilih.

Perhatikan urutannya: soal 1 baris 3, soal 2 baris 4, soal 3 baris 8, soal 4 baris 12, soal 5 baris 17. Tidak pernah mundur. Kalau kamu kehilangan soal 3, jawaban soal 4 masih di depan — asal matamu sudah pindah ke pilihan soal 4 sebelum baris 12 diucapkan.
